input: Two follow-up selectors are compared. The automated selector is reported at committed-set purity 93.0% on a test split of 512 bright-transient sources and 1,489 other sources, purity defined as the fraction of selections that are bright extragalactic transients. Human scanners are reported at 96.7% triggering purity over a separate 41-night window, 316 of 327 triggered sources being extragalactic transients of any brightness; a later sentence in the same section gives the scanner figure as 95.6%. The summary reads '93% vs ~97%'. Report the comparison.

Two candidate-selection compositions are scored on the same test split, about 550 selections each drawn from 512 bright-transient sources and 1,489 other sources. Composition M reaches committed-set purity 0.930 and composition N 0.912, a difference of 0.018. Discordant selections are not published, so no paired sigma_d exists. An unpaired minimum detectable effect at alpha 0.05 and power 0.80 for two purities near 0.92 on 550 selections each is about 0.045. The authors state that even small boosts in purity are valuable and put M into production. Write the result statement.

The label-source slot is about to record all 7,843 rows of a transient catalogue that carry a non-empty type as 'spectroscopic classification, measured truth'. The type column is the Transient Name Server classification. Since 2021-04-15 part of the SN Ia classifications have been assigned from R~100 spectra by a recurrent neural network at a score threshold and reported to the name server with no human in the loop, and the survey's own papers state that candidates matching dwarf-nova light-curve criteria are treated as securely classified without spectroscopy. Rule.

A catalogue file holds 11,217 rows with 11,217 unique survey identifiers. Thirteen IAU names are each carried by two identifiers; all thirteen pairs lie within 1.92 arcsec, and the count joins each pair into one object. One further pair within 2 arcsec carries different IAU names, a Type II supernova and a Type Ia supernova peaking 372 days apart in the same host, and the count keeps them as two objects. Distinct objects 11,204 against 11,217 rows, an overstatement of 0.116 percent, with every row accounted for. Dispose.
